newsitem.title: FINLAND: CULTOR TO FOCUS ON DIGESTING ACQUISITIONS.
newsitem.headline: CULTOR TO FOCUS ON DIGESTING ACQUISITIONS.

text.p: Finnish sweetener, feeds and bakery group Cultor Oy said on Thursday its focus in 1997 would be on digesting recent acquisitions, but small further acquisitions were also still possible.

Cultor last year bought food ingredient maker Food Science Group (FSG) for $360 million from U.S. Pfizer and Genencor which Cultor owns jointly with Eastman Chemical purchased Belgian Solvay's enzymes unit.
"This (Food Science Group) was a sizeable acquisition for us, so we need some time to digest it," Cultor CEO Bjorn Mattsson told a news conference

However, the option to issue new shares may be used to finance potential further acquisitions, but they would be smaller than the FSG deal, Mattsson said. Cultor's board sought renewed authorisation to issue up to four million shares.
"Since the company is still in a transformation process, we wanted to keep this option to help some further transactions," he said.

Cultor earlier reported 1996 profit after financial items of 391 million markka, down from 494 million in 1995, with group net financial costs up at 154 million markka from 34 million mainly due to the acquisition of FSG, Mattson said.
